A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WyFormer study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original crystal-generation and property-prediction experiments, with additional timing, representation-ablation, LLM and token analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds a 10,000-structure DFT evaluation, SymmCD comparisons, generation ablations and initialization-variability measurements.

M1.justification: The Transformer architecture, element/site-symmetry/enumeration representation, autoregressive cascade, augmentation and structure-generation routes are retained. The new pseudocode documents the existing procedure. Harmonic-cluster generation was already proposed in v1 Appendix P; v3 adds its evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions use MP-20, its binary/ternary subset, MPTS-52, AFLOW and 3DSC for the same generation and property-prediction tasks. The larger DFT sample and new ablations remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: SymmCD changes from a cited work in v1 to an evaluated comparator in v3 Tables 1, 2 and 7. Table 12 also introduces a letter-based WyFormer generation control. The established external generators, property predictors and WyLLM comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 replaces the stated custom high-precision DFT workflow with a Materials Project double-relaxation/static workflow and changes the DFT reference hull. It adds a 10,000-structure evaluation with CHGNet pre-relaxation, a zero-meV stability threshold and train-only novelty reference, alongside the 105-structure evaluation. It also compares single versus double relaxation and specifies uniform 1,000-structure subsampling for Table 7 COV-P.

E4.justification: v3 adds a generation ablation comparing Wyckoff letters with site symmetry plus enumeration, tests the previously proposed harmonic-cluster generator, analyzes energy variability across random initializations, and evaluates sensitivity to DFT workflow. These substantially extend v1's retained property-encoding, LLM and diversity analyses.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 8 newly reports energy standard deviations across six pyXtal initializations for 1,000 representations, including a mean standard deviation of 0.14 eV/atom. Six initializations were already specified in v1; this is new variability reporting, not an increased run count. The p = 0.1 significance convention is retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the 105-structure S.U.N. rates, including WyFormer/CHGNet from 6.9% to 23.1% and WyFormerDiffCSP++ from 12.8% to 22.2%, under revised DFT settings. v3 adds 10,000-structure S.U.N. results of 3.83% and 4.14% for different relaxation protocols, SymmCD and ablation results, and WyLLM stability scores. Table 7 also revises COV-P values; Tables 3–4 property-prediction scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The harmonic-descriptor formula is corrected between v1 Appendix C and v3 Section 2.1.1: v1 repeats h^(1) and takes an imaginary part after a real-part operation, whereas v3 concatenates real and imaginary parts using both h^(1) and h^(2). The remaining harmonic derivation is largely relocated, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The six stated contributions and headline claims remain. The abstract qualifies the earlier suggestion that symmetry is unaccounted for to being often inadequately addressed. Section 3.1.4 adds a 24% S.U.N. advantage claim for the new large-sample comparison and removes the claim that WyFormer alone demonstrated generation up to 52 atoms per unit cell.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix H.1 adds a substantive qualification about comparing stability scores obtained with different DFT workflows. The earlier warning that Materials Project relaxation settings are too coarse is removed, and nonconvergence is described as instability for S.U.N. accounting rather than proof of unrealistic structures. The central entropy, novelty and stoichiometry limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, generation/training/forward-pass pseudocode, Spglib preprocessing information, VASP version and workflow identifiers, and an identifiable DFT hull file. Appendix E expands timing details and discloses disabling atom-type inference in the DiffCSP++ integration. Existing model hyperparameter lists are retained.

R1.justification: The principal positioning against diffusion models and earlier Wyckoff representations is retained. v3 adds references concerning spherical-harmonic descriptors, Wyckoff augmentation, Spglib, atomate2, pymatgen and Matbench Discovery, while removing Dudarev and Monkhorst–Pack citations associated with the old DFT description. The MatterGen publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Method exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized: spherical harmonics move from an appendix into Section 2.1.1, tokenization explanations are rewritten, and Appendix B expands into three algorithms. The abstract, evaluation narrative, DFT description and inference-speed discussion are also revised, beyond routine copyediting.

P2.justification: The tokenization diagram is redrawn, and the training diagram is redesigned and moved into the main text. v3 adds a generation flowchart, initialization-variability histogram and Wyckoff-position comparison display. Table 1 gains explicit protocol columns, Table 11 gains stability columns, and a generation-ablation table is added. Many earlier plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v1's central stability comparison relied on 105 structures per method and explicitly could not distinguish leading models. v3 substantially strengthens evaluation through the larger DFT study, explicit protocol-comparability analysis, SymmCD comparison and direct generation ablations. Code-access information and expanded procedural documentation also improve reproducibility. Reporting remains imperfect—Table 6 retains old S.U.N. rates despite Table 1's revisions, and several cross-references are incorrect—but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and transparency.
